description: Composite TEM figure for the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C low-density steel annealed at 800 °C, consisting of a bright-field micrograph plus three selected-area diffraction patterns. (a) Bright-field TEM image with phase labels printed in colour: "γ" (upper left), "α" (upper right and lower right) and two rod-like/lamellar "κ" particles (centre and lower left) lying inside α; two scale bars appear at the bottom, "0.5 μm" (left) and "500 nm" (right), indicating the field was assembled from two different magnifications. (b) Three indexed SADPs shown side by side: α at zone axis z = [111] with reflections labelled (10-1), (1-10), (0-11) around the transmitted beam T; κ at z = [001] with (100) and (110); γ at z = [011] with (11-1), (200) and (1-11) about T. Together the panels argue that in the 800 °C specimen the κ-carbide rods/globules embedded in α are incoherent: the citing text states several areas were examined and no orientation relationship was found between κ-carbide and its neighbouring α phase, unlike the Nishiyama–Wasserman relationship reported for 700 °C.

subfigures.description: TEM bright-field image of the 800 °C annealed specimen showing a large γ region at upper left, α grains at upper right and lower right, and two bright rod-like/lamellar κ-carbide particles within α (centre and lower left). Two scale bars are printed: '0.5 μm' (lower left) and '500 nm' (lower right).
Three selected-area diffraction patterns displayed side by side for the phases in (a), labelled α (z = [111]), κ (z = [001]) and γ (z = [011]).
SADP of α along z = [111]; labelled reflections (10-1), (1-10) and (0-11) with the transmitted beam marked T; faint additional spots are present.
SADP of κ-carbide along z = [001]; labelled reflections (100) and (110) either side of the transmitted beam T.
SADP of γ along z = [011]; labelled reflections (11-1), (200) and (1-11) around the transmitted beam T.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a TEM bright-field micrograph with in-image phase labels 'γ' (upper left), 'α' (upper right and lower right) and 'κ' (two rod-like particles, centre and lower left).
Panel (a) carries two separate scale bars printed along the bottom edge: '0.5 μm' on the left and '500 nm' on the right.
Panel (b) comprises three SADPs labelled α (z = [111]), κ (z = [001]) and γ (z = [011]).
In the α SADP, spots are indexed (10-1), (1-10) and (0-11) around the transmitted beam marked T.
In the κ SADP, spots are indexed (100) and (110) either side of the transmitted beam T.
In the γ SADP, spots are indexed (11-1), (200) and (1-11) around the transmitted beam T.
In panel (a) the κ-carbide appears as bright, elongated rod-like/lamellar particles embedded within the α matrix, while γ occupies a distinct background region.
The caption states that Fig. 8 shows the TEM micrograph of the specimen annealed at 800 °C, with (a) the BF image and (b) the SADPs of α, γ and κ in (a).
The citing text states that several areas were examined in this specimen and no orientation relationship was found between κ-carbide and its neighbouring α phase.
The citing text contrasts this with the 700 °C specimen (Fig. 7), where a Nishiyama–Wasserman (N–W) orientation relationship between lamellar κ-carbide and α matrix was identified.
The citing text states that κ-carbide with globular or short-rod-like shape shows no orientation relationship with the α matrix, and that coarsening of κ-carbide can destroy the coherency.
The citing text states that in the 800 °C specimen (Fig. 6(b)) the κ-carbide is larger, lower in fraction and closer to globular in shape than at 700 °C.
